headline: Spectral separation of overlapping optical components from measured image intensities
label: Spectral Unmixing And Segmentation
summary: Recent preprints apply physics-informed networks and phasor analysis to unmix overlapping optical spectra in photoacoustic and fluorescence imaging.
synthesis: The common thread is computational separation of overlapping spectral components in optical imaging, with decomposition driven by measured intensities together with physical or spectral structure rather than tissue-level annotation. SPOI-AE, a physics-informed autoencoder, performs nonlinear optical inversion and spectral unmixing of in vivo mouse lymph node photoacoustic images. The RGB phasor method applies a discrete Fourier transform to pixel intensities from RGB camera data on a commercial microscope, enabling unsupervised unmixing in fluorescence microscopy and brightfield segmentation in histology. BEEP learning, a multi-view tensor-based generalized linear model, unmixes multiple fluorophores by combining emission spectra and excitation variability. What is new is the use of modeled spectral structure to drive separation, extended to RGB camera data on a commercial microscope and to highly multiplexed fluorescence imaging. The modalities are heterogeneous, and segmentation is addressed only in the phasor study.
